the choice of θ and its effect on stability of stochastic θ-method for stochastic delay differential equation.
the stability of stochastic θ-method for SDEs without the linear growth of drift coefficients.

the stochastic θmethod can capture the stability in the sense of almost sure exponential stability for θ∊(1/2, 1] and the stability cannot be captured for θ∊[0, ½).
the θ-method with 1/2<θ≤1 can preserve the almost sure stability, while the θ-method with θ∈[θ, 1/ 2) cannot.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the stochastic θ method can capture the stability when the drift term is linearly growing and the stability is almost sure, but it may not capture the stability for non-linear growth drift and/or for the stability in the mean square sense.
the BEM and stochastic θ-method with θ∈(0.5, 1] are the most suitable methods for the almost sure stability.
the BEM method is the most robust numerical scheme to capture the almost sure stability and the stochastic θ-method for θ∈[1/2,1] is the second robust method.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of θ is very important to reproduce the stability of exact solution.
the stability of the stochastic θ-method depends on the choice of the parameter θ.
the stochastic θ method is more stable than the EM method, and the stability of the stochastic θ method depends on the choice of θ.
